Managing State

React components can hold local state between renders. The useState hook returns a pair: the current value and a function that updates it.

App.js
import { useState } from "react";
export default function Counter() {
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
function handleClick() {
setCount(count + 1);
}
return (
<button onClick={handleClick}>
Clicked {count} times
</button>
);
}

Calling the setter schedules a re-render. React batches updates that happen inside the same event handler, so the component renders only once.

Theming

A theme describes colours and typography for the whole application. Wrap the tree in a provider so descendants can read it without passing props.

App.js
const theme = createTheme({
palette: {
primary: { main: "#1976d2" },
secondary: { main: "#dc004e" },
},
typography: {
fontFamily: "Roboto, sans-serif",
fontSize: 14,
},
});
export default function App() {
return (
<ThemeProvider theme={theme}>
<Button variant="contained">Hello</Button>
</ThemeProvider>
);
}

That covers the basics of local state and theming. The next section looks at how updates propagate through the component tree.
